sections.subtitle: Baidu renamed its segment reporting partway through FY2024, so the two breakdowns below cover non-overlapping period ranges, not the same lines under new labels.

charts.title: Core Online vs Non-Online Marketing vs iQIYI
charts.annotation: Core online/non-online split was retired after FY2024; see the AI-powered business breakdown for FY2024-FY2025.

charts.title: AI-Powered Business: Applications vs AI-Native Marketing
charts.annotation: New segmentation introduced FY2024; only two FY points exist so far -- too early to trend, but the FY2024->FY2025 jump is the AI-monetisation signal the thesis rests on.

charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

legacyMix.title: Core online vs non-online marketing vs iQIYI
legacyMix.content:
Core online marketing is the legacy search/feed advertising business. Core non-online marketing was Baidu's prior label for AI Cloud and other non-ad Core revenue. iQIYI is the separately-listed streaming segment, consolidated but economically distinct.

For Baidu, Inc.: online marketing revenue has been shrinking (RMB75.1bn FY2023 → RMB73.0bn FY2024) as ad budgets shift to AI-native formats and macro ad demand softens, while non-online marketing grew (RMB28.4bn → RMB31.7bn) -- the mix shift the whole investment case depends on. Baidu retired this split after FY2024 in favour of the AI-powered-business breakdown in the next chart, so FY2025 has no comparable cells here.

What to watch:

  • Whether online marketing's decline is stabilising or accelerating
  • iQIYI's revenue trend as a standalone, lower-margin check on consolidated numbers
  • The FY2024 handoff point into the new AI-powered-business reporting

aiBusiness.title: AI-powered business: applications vs AI-native marketing
aiBusiness.content:
Baidu's current segmentation: AI-powered business is the total (AI Cloud + AI-native marketing + other AI applications); AI applications and AI-native marketing are its two disclosed components.

For Baidu, Inc.: AI-powered business revenue grew from RMB27.0bn (FY2024) to RMB40.0bn (FY2025), with AI-native marketing more than tripling (RMB2.4bn → RMB9.8bn) -- the clearest evidence yet that AI features are monetising inside the core ad product rather than just adding cloud revenue. Only two FY points exist since Baidu only started this breakdown in FY2024; a trend call needs another year of data.

What to watch:

  • AI-native marketing's share of total marketing revenue rising further
  • Whether AI-powered-business growth is cannibalising legacy search ads or additive
  • Quarterly cadence (ERNIE 4.5/5.0 rollout, Apollo Go scaling) once more FY history accumulates

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Baidu, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Baidu, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Baidu, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Baidu, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Baidu, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Baidu, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Baidu, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Baidu, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Baidu, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Baidu, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
